issues.source_quote: Нет, я никуда не еду. Мы провожаем папу!!!
issues.translation_quote: We're seeing Daddy off! - Oh! What was that for? - You can't do that!
issues.justification: Garbled dialogue structure: the child's line, the following 'Ой! Ну что же это такое' and 'Ну разве можно' are mangled, and the rendering misattributes and confuses speakers.

issues.translation_quote: Fris Street, Fish Street, - Chikanuk Pharmacy...
issues.justification: The mangled/parodic foreign-sounding street name and rehearsal of a spy cover is left opaque; the 'Fish' gloss is a mistranslation of a deliberate phonetic mock and the humor is lost.

issues.source_quote: Кон-тра-бан-да! ... Читали в «Неделе», отдел для, дома для семьи...
issues.translation_quote: Didn't you read it in The Week? The home-and-family section?
issues.justification: Cultural reference to the Soviet newspaper 'Nedelya' is left without any cue; also the doctors-recommend gag is lost for the target audience.

'Не актуально' is a dated Soviet idiom for 'out of fashion/irrelevant'; 'topical' is a stiff, wrong rendering. Also 'Ba-ba-ba' and 'Oh yes, be chill, all right' mistranslate the garbled pseudo-English 'О ес, би чел' (a joke of fake English).

issues.source_quote: Куй железо, не отходя от кассы!
issues.translation_quote: strike while the iron's hot— right at the cash register!
issues.justification: The Soviet comedic blend of proverb and 'don't leave the cash desk' is rendered literally; reads awkwardly, though it partially keeps the pun. Acceptable but clunky as a repeated catchphrase.

issues.source_quote: Вы ко мне приедете. Если мы Вам будем нужны… Я вызываю такси на своё имя.
issues.translation_quote: If we need you... You'll come to me. If you need us... I'll call a taxi in my name.
issues.justification: Roles reversed: the Russian says if he needs them, he calls a taxi in his own name; translation garbles who calls the taxi and the logic of the code.

issues.source_quote: Это - я, я, я! ... Щорт побери...
issues.justification: The running gag of foreigners mangling the password 'Чёрт побери' (Щёрт, Шьёрт) is flattened into a uniform 'Damn it', losing the comic accent.

issues.source_quote: Эти игрушки идиотские! ... Откуда у тебя пистолет и деньги?
issues.translation_quote: Is this yours? Mine... Where did it come from? Over there... Over there...
issues.justification: The Russian 'Оттуда' alludes to the West/abroad; ambiguous, but acceptable. More serious: 'Измена' translated as 'treason' for infidelity-confession shifts the meaning; Nadya means 'betrayal/espionage' conflated with adultery, and the pun is lost.

issues.source_quote: Хорошо, что он не контрабандист, симпатичный мужик
issues.translation_quote: I'm glad he's not a smuggler.
issues.justification: Minor loss of nuance, but also 'Ты зачем усы сбрил, дурик?' is fine. The larger issue is the omitted/odd ending lyric and 'Ну-ка иди отсюда, Миша! Как у вас там говорят, топай до хазы' rendered as 'get back to your pad' which loses the mock-criminal slang.

issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты исдох! Чтоб я видел тебя у гробу, у белых тапках! Чтоб ты жил на одну зарплату!
issues.translation_quote: Drop dead! I hope to see you in your coffin, in your little white slippers! May you live... on nothing... but your salary!
issues.justification: The neighbour's Odessa-style dialectal Yiddish-inflected speech ('у гробу, у белых тапках') is rendered in standard English, losing the character voice.

issues.translation_quote: Everything we agreed... We whip off the cast and clear out!
issues.justification: Lyolik's signature mock-Odessa/comic speech ('Усё', 'смываемося', 'Козладоев') is neutralized, flattening the villain's distinctive voice.
Fine, but 'Кутузов!' as an exclamation after being hit is left unexplained and reads as a non-sequitur; the one-eyed-general reference is lost.

issues.source_quote: Не взял попутных - это не таксист! Бандит!
issues.translation_quote: He won't pick up passengers. He's no taxi driver! He's a bandit!
issues.justification: 'Let's give them a ride' / 'Not allowed, regulations' is fine, but the logic is slightly muddled; 'It's not a taxi driver' loses 'didn't pick up fares along the way'.

issues.source_quote: Ну что же это такое... - Ну разве можно!...
issues.translation_quote: What was that for? - You can't do that!
issues.justification: Unnatural rendering of a reaction to the child's behavior; 'What was that for?' misreads the exclamation.
Stiff and unidiomatic; natural English would be 'My eye's fine, it'll heal'.

issues.source_quote: Кто возьмёт билетов пачку, тот получит... Водокачку!
issues.translation_quote: Buy a stack of tickets, win a fabulous... waterworks!
issues.justification: The Russian rhyme (пачку/водокачку) is lost and 'fabulous' is an addition; the comic anticlimax is weakened.

issues.source_quote: Такова «сё ля ви», как говорят у них...
issues.translation_quote: Such is "say lah vee," as they say over there...
issues.justification: Phonetic respelling is awkward in English; the pretentious tone is partly lost.
Soviet slogan-like register is weakly conveyed; reads as plain imperative.

issues.source_quote: Шампанское по утрам пьют или аристократы, или дегенераты!
issues.translation_quote: Only aristocrats and degenerates drink champagne in the morning!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the official Soviet moralizing tone of the building manager could be sharper.
